facts.value: Dockerfile builds, Prime Images, and Docker Hub images; VM builds require linux/amd64
facts.notes: Other public registries are not accepted directly by sandbox create: transfer supported public sources into Prime first. Allowed sources include GHCR, Quay, public ECR, registry.k8s.io, and MCR; Google-hosted registries are rejected. Private-source registry credentials and image/build-context size ceilings are not established. Guides say first VM conversion can take a few minutes in PENDING; Harbor instead says ~10 minutes for first VM builds. Source-image push performs conversion before launch. Docker Hub source builds become PUBLIC platform images and cannot use custom destination/team/private visibility; do not generalize private-by-default Dockerfile images to those imports. Image storage and a one-day-storage upload charge apply separately. Marketing calls task artifacts immutable, but logical image retag/rename is supported; upstream mutable-tag refresh is not specified.

facts.value: By baking a Docker image, or by running commands in the sandbox
facts.notes: No separate package API was named.

facts.value: Commands use the configured guest user, normally root
facts.notes: Released SDK README explicitly says normally root when user is omitted; this is guest access, not host privilege or guaranteed sudo in every custom image. Per-command user selection requires supporting sandboxd; older guests can ignore the field and execute as their default user, so upgrade or recreate them. Named accounts must already exist.

facts.value: VM sandboxes support Docker
facts.notes: Overview also names systemd, background services, and kernel-dependent workloads.

facts.value: Background jobs survive the command connection, not sandbox termination
facts.notes: start_background_job runs across API calls until completion or sandbox termination. A start_command process stops the sandbox when it exits; omit it to keep the sandbox available for commands. Lifetime and optional idle timeout still apply. Checkpoint/fork preserves files only, not running jobs or memory.

facts.value: upload_file, download_file, and read_file
facts.notes: Uploads are limited to 16 MiB per file. Reads are size-limited; download_file is the path for larger files.

facts.value: Explicit durable filesystem checkpoint and restore into a new sandbox
facts.notes: A DURABLE checkpoint outlives its source sandbox; root-disk attachment or automatic latest-file persistence after termination is not established. Keep the source running until DURABLE: deletion or timeout first loses the checkpoint. Restore uses checkpoint_id without docker_image or disk_size_gb, which come from the checkpoint. Files only, not processes/memory. Stored checkpoints incur separate storage and upload charges; retention TTL is not published in the guides.

facts.value: Files-only checkpoints of running sandboxes; restore into new sandboxes after DURABLE
facts.notes: Files only, not running processes or memory. Wait for DURABLE before deleting or allowing the source to time out; earlier termination loses the checkpoint. A DURABLE checkpoint outlives its source. Restore omits docker_image and disk_size_gb; resources, environment variables, and timeouts can be configured. Storage costs $0.10 per GiB per month billed hourly, plus a one-time upload charge equal to one day of storage when DURABLE. No numeric checkpoint latency, consistency guarantee, or retention TTL is published in the guides. The September 23 launch blog's coming-soon wording predates the released checkpoint feature and current guides.

facts.value: prime sandbox fork checkpoints files and starts a new sandbox
facts.notes: Fork waits for the checkpoint to be saved; keep the source alive until DURABLE. Files copy, but processes start fresh and memory is not carried over. CPU, memory, and timeout inherit unless overridden; --wait-timeout caps the wait, not a published fork benchmark. Checkpoint storage/upload charges apply; an in-place reset primitive is not documented.

facts.value: Unrestricted when no policy is set in the released CLI; explicit deny-all includes DNS
facts.notes: Released CLI describes unset allowlist/denylist as Unrestricted; SDK network_allowlist=[] denies all egress including DNS. Harbor's no-network integration mode retains framework interception/MCP routes and keeps trusted setup online, so it is not identical to raw Sandbox deny-all. Authorized inference/proxy services can fetch remotely outside the sandbox boundary; network policy is not an end-to-end offline guarantee.

facts.value: VM egress allowlist or denylist, mutually exclusive; deny-all includes DNS
facts.notes: Released SDK permits at most 256 entries: exact hostnames, leftmost-label wildcard domains, IPv4/CIDRs; rejects IPv6, schemes, credentials, ports, paths, query strings, and bare '*'. CLI --deny '*' is a special deny-all shortcut, not an SDK list entry. Runtime updates replace the whole list; verify applied state because saved rules may lag. DNS/SNI and protocol enforcement details remain unestablished. Harbor may add framework routes and keeps trusted setup online; authorized remote-fetch services are outside sandbox egress control, not proof of a VM-policy bypass.

Retained unknown for general Sandbox ingress because positive official evidence has unclear applicability, not merely because docs omit it. The official Prime Agent reference (last file commit 2026-09-30, reviewed 2026-10-08) says Tunnel exposes local or in-sandbox services; exact Sandbox/evaluation guides only establish opted-in hosted-evaluation forwarding. General arbitrary-Sandbox eligibility/access and raw TCP remain unresolved after audit Q4/P4 and full API/SDK review. --allow-tunnel-access grants the hosted run's temporary key permissions; SSH explicitly lacks -L/-R forwarding. Do not generalize evaluation-only support into unrestricted general ingress.

Retained unknown for general Sandbox preview URLs because official positive scope is unclear: Prime Agent's reference says local or in-sandbox services, while exact product guides affirm only caller-local and opted-in hosted-evaluation HTTPS tunnels. Reviewed 2026-10-08 via audit Q4/P4 and full API/SDK passages; this is not simple absent documentation. Confirmed evaluation tunnels use t-<id>.tunnel.pinfra.io, public by default, optional Basic Auth with a generated password shown once, and an active client. General Sandbox bind/TLS/lifetime/access contract remains unresolved.

facts.value: 1 minute to unlimited, default 60 minutes
facts.notes: A negative timeout means no lifetime deadline. A finite timeout must be at least as long as the idle timeout.

facts.value: Disabled by default; 1 to 1,440 minutes when set
facts.notes: Command, upload, download, and file-read calls reset it. SSH does not. Long-running execs stay pinned for their duration.

facts.value: 102,400 sandbox creations per hour, with a burst of 192 per 10 seconds
facts.notes: Account defaults, not per-sandbox throughput. The SDK list polling backs off on throttling; other sandbox endpoint rates are not published in the guides. Image builds separately allow 150 requests per 60 seconds per IP and token, with additional unpublished per-image account source-build limits. Tunnel endpoint rates are a separate service.

facts.value: Optional SDK region and CLI --region selector; available-region inventory unknown
facts.notes: Released create model accepts region; CLI help gives us and eu-west as examples and uses the backend default when omitted. These examples do not establish currently available regions, residency guarantees, regional capacity, or regional pricing. Overview/product marketing and public OpenAPI do not supply a Sandbox region inventory.

facts.value: Released Python SDK open_process streams VM process stdout/stderr and accepts stdin
facts.notes: CLI v0.9.4 / prime-sandboxes 0.4.3 source exposes a live process handle with exit wait and terminate/kill. Reattachment does not replay output emitted while detached. Async process stdout/stderr are byte iterators; the protocol has no stdin-EOF operation. This is not process-memory restore after sandbox termination.

facts.value: prime sandbox logs / SDK get_logs, command output, and polled background-job output
facts.notes: Released SDK GET /api/v1/sandbox/{id}/logs retrieves backend logs. Background-job retrieval returns at most the last 10 MiB of each stream with truncation flags; output errors are independent of exit status. Log retention/search and survival-after-delete guarantees remain unestablished. Hosted-evaluation log storage is a separate workflow.

facts.value: prime sandbox ssh interactive guest shell
facts.notes: Requires a RUNNING sandbox and local OpenSSH. The CLI generates an ephemeral key/session and revokes/deletes it on disconnect; shell defaults to /bin/sh as the guest default user. SSH does not reset idle timeout and does not support port/agent forwarding, scp, or sftp. A separate PTY API is not established.

facts.value: Encrypted secrets injected as environment variables
facts.notes: Secrets are not returned in API responses. Plain environment variables are separate and are stored in plain text.

facts.value: Permission-scoped API keys, team context, and admin-scoped bulk deletion
facts.notes: API keys can expire and be revoked. CLI --all-users and --user bulk deletion are team-admin-only; --all defaults to the caller's sandboxes. Labels are organizational filters, not authorization boundaries. Full Sandbox role matrix, SSO, and audit-log guarantees are not established.

cloning_forking.note: prime sandbox fork checkpoints files, waits for durability, and starts a new sandbox. Processes start fresh; CPU/memory/timeout inherit unless overridden. Source must remain alive until DURABLE; checkpoint storage/upload charges apply.

persistent_filesystem.note: Explicit DURABLE filesystem checkpoints outlive their source and restore into new sandboxes. Automatic root-disk persistence after termination is not established; keep the source alive until DURABLE. Files only; storage/upload charges apply.

volumes.note: NO DOCUMENTED SUPPORT FOUND: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08. Scope: Sandbox docs, marketing, released models/client/samples, storage/mount searches and disk API navigation (audit Q3/Q8 and policy follow-up). Conservative audit inference, not an explicit vendor denial. Per-sandbox disk/checkpoints, Hosted Training volumes and GPU-instance disks do not count.

custom_images.note: Dockerfile or accepted public-registry source builds create linux/amd64 VM artifacts. Other registries need transfer into Prime; Google-hosted registries are rejected. Docker Hub source builds force PUBLIC platform scope, unlike private-by-default Dockerfile builds. First conversion can take minutes; storage/upload charges apply.

docker_in_sandbox.note: VM sandboxes, the default runtime, support Docker, systemd, and background services.

root_sudo.note: Released SDK says commands use the configured guest user, normally root. Not host access or guaranteed sudo in every image. Per-command user selection requires supporting sandboxd; older guests can ignore it and run as the default user.

gpu.note: No open GPU Sandbox tier is established: coming soon, VM-only, explicit Prime grant required, and >0 errors without access. The 0-to-8 table is not availability; sibling GPU compute/training/inference does not count.

open_source.note: Prime CLI/SDK monorepo and prime-sandboxes client are MIT. No open hosted runtime/server or self-host deployment is established.

background_processes.note: Background jobs survive API calls until completion or sandbox termination, not checkpoint/fork memory restore. A start_command exit stops the sandbox; lifetime and optional idle timeout still apply.

terminal_pty.note: prime sandbox ssh opens an interactive guest shell on a RUNNING sandbox with local OpenSSH and an ephemeral key/session revoked on disconnect. SSH does not reset idle timeout; no SSH port/agent forwarding, scp, or sftp. Separate PTY API unestablished.

command_streaming.note: Released prime-sandboxes 0.4.3 open_process streams VM stdout/stderr, writes stdin, waits for exit, and signals processes. Output emitted while detached is not replayed; protocol has no stdin-EOF operation. Not memory recovery.

secrets_management.note: Secrets are encrypted at rest, injected as environment variables, and not returned in API responses.

python_sdk.note: The official client is the Python package prime_sandboxes, with sync and async clients.

pricing_summary: Prime Sandboxes running launch rates are valid through December 22, 2026: CPU $0.02 per vCPU per hour, memory $0.0125 per GiB per hour, and disk $0.0002 per GiB per hour. The overview prints 1 vCPU, 2 GiB RAM, 5 GiB disk as $0.046/hour. Product marketing states no subscriptions or minimum spend. VM images/checkpoints cost $0.10 per GiB per month, billed hourly while they exist, plus a one-time upload charge equal to one day of storage when an image build completes or checkpoint becomes DURABLE. Running includes waiting/idle time; active-CPU metering and pause are not established. Compute rounding/minimum increments, egress/ingress/storage I/O, additional build charges, allowances, and post-launch rates remain unknown. Insufficient account balance raises PaymentRequiredError.

Released SDK delete_checkpoint stops its billing, may retain data for descendants, and returns HTTP 409 while pending or the active tip of a running sandbox.

Regional price alternatives and post-December-22 compute rates remain unknown; wallet amounts are USD and published dollar/GiB units are preserved.

research_notes: The published CPU, memory, and disk rates are explicitly limited to December 22, 2026.

GPU count appears in the limits table, but GPU Sandboxes remain coming soon and >0 requests error without an explicit Prime grant. Sibling GPU instances, Hosted Training, and Inference do not establish Sandbox GPU eligibility.

Filesystem checkpoint/restore/fork is now documented and released (CLI 0.9.2 / prime-sandboxes 0.4.2, 2026-10-02); CLI 0.9.4 / prime-sandboxes 0.4.3 adds checkpoint deletion. Wait for DURABLE while keeping the source alive; files survive, processes/memory do not.

Official overview, SDK, CLI, images, tunnel, hosted-evaluation scope, public OpenAPI, product marketing, and released client source were audited on 2026-10-08. SDK license and guest root/streaming evidence do not establish a self-hosted server.

The 2026-10-08T03:44Z capability eligibility policy was applied per field after additional official docs/marketing/SDK/API searches. NO DOCUMENTED SUPPORT FOUND audit inferences classify self-host/BYOC, community/TypeScript/Go SDKs, general private networking, attachable volumes, pause/resume and separate memory recovery as unsupported/false, not explicit vendor denials. General HTTPS ingress/preview remains unknown because official Prime Agent in-sandbox tunnel wording has unclear general-product applicability; confirmed hosted-evaluation forwarding remains partial. Numeric pricing/limits/retention, available-region inventory, checkpoint consistency and undisclosed restrictions remain unknown. No paid API execution or independent benchmark was performed.

The September 23, 2026 launch blog still calls snapshots/forks forthcoming; current overview (sitemap lastmod October 6) and released CLI/SDK document filesystem checkpoints. Current file-only recovery supersedes that dated roadmap, not the blog's possible future memory/shared-workspace features. GPU examples in the released examples README do not override the explicit coming-soon/grant gate.
